newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork belly futures calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork belly futures calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while expectations on pork bellies ranged from 0.250 cent lower to 0.100 higher, livestock analysts said.

Some analysts expect early pressure following steady to lower cash hog indications. Hog marketings were up to start the week, as rain moved through the Midwest late Sunday and early Monday and curbed the last of farmers' fieldwork. Also, packers were holding bids down in the face of declining pork cutout values.
However, others look for support to develop as hog supplies were seen tightening in the near term.
Hog numbers are expected to decline seasonally and cash markets may turn up as the week wears on, sources said.

Pork belly futures indications were also mixed with some analysts looking for carryover selling following sharp losses late last week. Hog slaughter was heavy last week which may prompt carryover selling, especially with futures at a premium to cash, they said.
USDA estimated the week's hog slaughter last week at 1,649,000 head, above 1,631,000 a week earlier and 1,629,000 a year earlier.

However, others look for the rate of slaughter to ease during the week and the cash market to bottom. Tuesday's CME Out-of-Town and Friday's monthly USDA Cold Storage reports were also expected to be supportive to the market as stored supplies remain on the light side, they added.
